mAbs 2026-12-31 High

Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.

This paper benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated 200-complex dataset (SAbDab2-Bench) and a reconstructed Ab-FoldBench subset. The authors standardize inputs, sampling, and interface metrics to fairly compare docking accuracy and interaction specificity across models. The work provides a much-needed standardized evaluation framework for antibody-antigen co-folding beyond AlphaFold 3.

Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.

This study integrates human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, and molecular modeling to show that the endocrine-disrupting chemical 4-nonylphenol worsens allergic rhinitis by impairing IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation. Key genes IFNG and SKIL were downregulated in AR patients while CDKN1A was upregulated, with IFNG expression concentrated in T-cells. The findings suggest a mechanistic link between environmental chemical exposure and allergic disease via disrupted immune signaling.

Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.

This study combines sequence homology searches with structural modeling of binding pockets to identify candidate 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylases in phylogenetically diverse gut bacteria, expanding beyond the few known urolithin A-producing species. The approach leverages pocket conservation to prioritize enzymes that sequence alone would miss, offering new leads for understanding how gut microbes convert dietary polyphenols into bioactive urolithin A.

Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.

This study shows that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) contain information about alternative protein conformations, even when the model outputs a single structure from a deep multiple sequence alignment. By analyzing these multi-modal distance distributions, the authors demonstrate that structural heterogeneity is encoded within standard AF2 predictions and can be used to predict an alternative conformation of a known protein structure.

This addresses the poor activity of natural enzymes with alternative cofactors, offering a more efficient alternative to directed evolution and rational design for cost-effective biocatalysis.

Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.

This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how a naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor crystal transitions between two polymorphs (α at room temperature, γ at higher temperatures). The simulations reproduce both stable phases and refine unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations that were only partially resolved experimentally, showing the α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving fast and slow molecular motions.

Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.

This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to compute potential of mean force (PMF) profiles that predict how diverse PFAS molecules partition into phospholipid bilayers. By integrating interaction energies along defined pathways, the approach offers a physics-based way to estimate membrane partitioning for PFAS with varied headgroups and fluorinated tails, which is otherwise difficult given their chemical diversity. The work provides a computational framework linking PFAS structure to membrane accumulation relevant to cellular health.

Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.

This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for modeling graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on how electrode-charging approaches (fixed/constant-charge, constant potential, and electronic-structure-aware methods) capture interfacial structure and capacitance. It argues that molecular-scale simulations are essential because neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales. The review serves as a methodological guide for computational electrochemistry of carbon-based energy storage interfaces.

Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.

This paper uses correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED-CCSD) to revisit theoretical predictions that strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities can invert the intrinsic regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. The authors confirm substantial energetic reordering of the Wheland intermediates, supporting the concept of a 'photonic substituent effect' that can control ground-state chemical reactivity through cavity-induced electronic and structural changes.

They find that the information content of these observables varies, with some techniques better able to discriminate between the different theoretical predictions.

Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference.

The approach aims to better distinguish genuine physical features in free energy profiles from artifacts caused by inadequate sampling or insufficient data. It provides a more robust statistical foundation for assessing the reliability of free energy predictions from molecular dynamics simulations.

MARS: Machine-Learned Force Field Framework for Automated Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation.

MARS is an open-source Python package that automates conformational ensemble generation, infrared spectrum prediction, and explicit microsolvation using machine-learned force fields (SO3LR, MACE) with GPU acceleration via JAX. It combines metadynamics, multitemperature molecular dynamics, and genetic algorithms in a four-phase sampling workflow, and includes automated vibrational mode classification via Wilson B-matrix projections. The tool aims to make MLFF-based spectroscopy and solvation studies accessible without manual workflow construction.

Orf virus early genes ORFV113 and ORFV114 are individually dispensable for replication in vitro but required for full virulence in vivo.

This study shows that the Orf virus genes ORFV113 and ORFV114, located in the variable terminal region of the genome, are not needed for the virus to replicate in cultured lamb testis cells, as single-gene deletion mutants grew normally in vitro. However, deleting either gene reduced the virus's ability to cause disease in the natural host, indicating both contribute to full virulence. The work characterizes their transcription and uses homologous recombination to build reporter-tagged deletion mutants.

PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design.

The authors introduce PFM (perturbed flow matching), a generative framework for structure-based drug design that overcomes the restriction of diffusion models to closed-form marginal distributions. By using flow matching with a perturbed forward process, PFM allows more flexible design of the noising process, potentially better capturing the complex pocket-conditioned molecular distributions. This addresses a key limitation of existing diffusion-based 3D molecular generation methods.

Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Cofolding Models: Correct Ligand Placement Is Decoupled From Accurate Protein Conformation.

This study benchmarks four leading AI cofolding models (AlphaFold3, RoseTTAFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1) on kinase and Class A GPCR complexes and finds that correct ligand placement is systematically decoupled from accurate prediction of the surrounding protein conformation. In other words, a model can put the ligand in the right spot even when the protein fold itself is mispredicted, so ligand accuracy alone is not evidence of a correct complex. The work cautions against judging cofolding models by ligand placement metrics alone.
